goal: Test whether an opaque synthetic plate and thagomizer seed can avoid the translucent-guide failure and be naturalized by RealVisXL i2i.

experiments.finding: Rejected as a direct app candidate. It replaces the transparent guide failure with countable opaque plates and visible tail spikes, but the base becomes a thick artificial back band.

experiments.type: RealVisXL i2i over opaque seed v1b
experiments.finding: Rejected. The model preserves the artificial back band and turns the plate row toward a shell or armored ridge instead of natural embedded Stegosaurus dorsal plates.

decision.reason: The opaque synthetic seed is clearer than the translucent route, but RealVisXL i2i still does not convert it into plausible Stegosaurus anatomy.
decision.nextRoute: Use opaque synthetic seeds only as LoRA/control training material after improving their base integration. Do not promote them directly or rely on plain i2i to solve plate integration.
